_comment: irrd-3a AC11 baseline for the title-extraction soft regression gate (and the surrounding src/scoring.py aggregates, for context). NULL placeholders until the first real eval run — that run needs OPENAI_API_KEY and ~10 min, so it is opt-in and never part of the fast CI path. While `title_extraction.title_extraction_f1` is null the gate in src/metrics/title_extraction.py passes with `baseline_missing: true` (nothing to regress against). Capture the PRE-confidence baseline with `EXTRACTOR_EMIT_CONFIDENCE=false npx nx run eval:confidence-gate -- --write-baseline`, then re-run with the flag on and compare: the run must stay within 5% relative of the value recorded here. Baseline is refreshed post-merge, not mid-story.
_emit_confidence_comment: Machine-readable form of _extractor_flag, stamped by --write-baseline. The gate run reports whether baseline-vs-run is AC11's real before/after (false -> true) or merely a like-for-like drift check; null means the baseline predates this field and the comparison cannot be shown to be a before/after.

title_extraction._comment: Token-level F1 between extracted and ground-truth recipe titles, averaged over fixtures. Distinct from scoring.metadata_accuracy, which blends title with prep/cook time and servings and therefore hides a title-only regression.

extraction_scores._comment: Aggregate means from src/fixture_runner._aggregate_scores ('<metric>_avg' keys). Context for interpreting a title movement — a title drop alongside an across-the-board drop is a different diagnosis than a title-only drop.

thresholds._note: Soft: not wired into the fast CI path. Blocking for this story — a >5% relative drop means the confidence-emitting prompts get retuned before irrd-3a completes.
